title: SOC 2 examination status, scope and use
status_rationale: Echelon has no SOC 2 report. Unbound defines a readiness directive (SOC2-001 onward) that explicitly is not a compliance claim, and CNV-GOV-001 requires evidence engineering from inception. No auditor is engaged.
target_answer: Echelon will obtain a SOC 2 Type I followed by a Type II examination covering Security and Availability, plus Confidentiality and Processing Integrity for Unbound, with a system description scoped to the named product, environment and legal entity. Controls emit evidence as a byproduct of operation (SOC2-004) so the observation period is cheap to evidence. Exceptions and opinion modifications are disclosed with remediation. We publish the complementary user entity controls customers must operate and the carved-out subservice organizations with how we monitor them. Assurance roadmap (the single timeline that ANS-AUD-002, ANS-FCT-004 and ANS-RCN-005 refer to): (1) readiness work by a party other than the examining CPA firm; (2) at production go-live, a SOC 2 Type I and, where a sponsor relies on Unbound for financial reporting, a SOC 1 Type 1, each as of a date when controls are placed in operation; (3) first Type 2 periods of at least three months, sized so the SOC 1 Type 2 covers as much of the first hosted sponsor's fiscal year as possible; (4) where go-live is less than roughly six to nine months before that sponsor's fiscal year end, no SOC 1 Type 2 can exist in time and the stated fallback is that the sponsor's auditor tests Unbound directly or performs substantive procedures, with Echelon cooperating and bearing the reasonable incremental cost of direct testing by agreement. None of this has started; no auditor is engaged.
current_practice: No SOC report; no auditor engaged.
intended_practice: Readiness through continuous evidence; Type I after first production release, Type II after a 6 to 12 month observation period.
customer_statement: Echelon does not have a SOC 2 or SOC 1 report and has not engaged an auditor. It plans a SOC 2 Type I and, for sponsors relying on Unbound for financial reporting, a SOC 1 Type 1 at production go-live, followed by Type 2 periods; where timing does not allow a SOC 1 Type 2 before a sponsor's fiscal year end, the sponsor's auditor would need to test directly or substantively. We will not claim SOC 2 or SOC 1 compliance before an auditor issues a report.

title: SOC 1 relevance for customers' financial reporting
status_rationale: CNV-GOV-001 requires evidence engineering for SOC 1 (AT-C 320, ledger and ICFR objectives); CNV-PLT-009 separates service-organization evidence including IPE run records. No SOC 1 exists.

Timing follows the assurance roadmap in ANS-AUD-001, including the fallback when a SOC 1 Type 2 cannot exist before a sponsor's fiscal year end.

title: Bridge letters and assurance coverage gaps
status_rationale: CNV-GOV-002 requires vendor assurance monitoring to compute the gap between a SOC period end and each relying party's fiscal year end. There is no report, so no bridge letter exists.
target_answer: Within 15 business days of request, Echelon issues a bridge letter signed by management covering the period from the report end date to the requested date, stating whether material changes to the system or controls occurred and whether any known deficiencies exist. Because a bridge letter is a management assertion, we supplement it with access to continuous control evidence for the gap period. Report periods are planned so the gap to customers' common fiscal year ends does not exceed three months.
current_practice: Not applicable yet; no report exists.
intended_practice: Template bridge letter and evidence feed once the first report is issued.
customer_statement: No SOC report exists, so no bridge letter is available. Bridge letters supplemented by continuous control evidence are planned.

challenge.customer_intent: Assurance covering the months between the audit period and the customer's reporting date.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Control failures in the gap period go unnoticed.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: A bridge letter is an unaudited management assertion; it adds little assurance beyond the vendor's word.
challenge.legally_required: No; auditors of public companies and some sponsors request them by practice.
challenge.contractually_required: Often requested in contracts with SOC reporting clauses.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Continuous control monitoring alerts on failures during the gap.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Read-only evidence feed of control runs for the gap period.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Bridge letter plus continuous evidence the customer can inspect.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Partially; evidence is first-party but tamper-evident and time-stamped.

title: ISO and other certifications and program authorizations
status_rationale: Echelon holds no ISO/IEC 27001, ISO/IEC 42001, CSA STAR, PCI, FedRAMP or StateRAMP certification or authorization. None is currently planned with a date.
target_answer: We hold certifications that our customers' requirements actually justify, chosen by evidence of customer demand rather than in advance. Likely sequence: CSA STAR Level 1 self-assessment (low cost, public CAIQ), then SOC 2, then ISO/IEC 27001 if international or enterprise demand appears, and ISO/IEC 42001 if AI governance assurance is demanded. Any certificate comes from an accredited certification body with its scope published. PCI DSS is out of scope while card acceptance is disabled (CNV-PAY-008); public-sector authorizations are not pursued unless a public-sector customer requires them.
intended_practice: Complete a CAIQ-based self-assessment once controls exist; decide on ISO from recorded customer demand.
customer_statement: Echelon does not hold ISO 27001, ISO 42001, CSA STAR, PCI DSS, FedRAMP or StateRAMP certification or authorization.

title: Independent technical assessment reports and labeling of first-party assessments
status_rationale: The Secure Construction Standard plans first-party assessment deliverables and states that external penetration testing remains planned for Unbound; it requires reports to be labeled first-party and never imply independent testing. No independent test has occurred.
target_answer: We share, under NDA, an attestation letter from an independent penetration tester with tester identity, qualifications, dates, scope and findings summary by severity with remediation status, at least annually and after major architecture change. First-party assessments (architectural assurance matrix, scanner validation, monthly assurance summary) are labeled first-party in their title and metadata. Customers may run their own security testing under an agreed rules-of-engagement document.
current_practice: No independent assessment performed; first-party report formats are proposed in the Standard.
intended_practice: Commission an independent test before production launch of Unbound.
customer_statement: No independent penetration test has been performed. One is planned before production launch. Any Echelon-authored assessment will be labeled first-party.

challenge.customer_intent: Independent evidence that the application resists attack.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Exploitable flaws exist that the vendor did not find.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Annual time-boxed pen tests are point-in-time and depend on tester skill; they miss many flaw classes but remain the expected independent signal.
challenge.legally_required: Not by statute for Echelon; some customers' regulations (for example NYDFS Part 500 for covered entities) require their own testing programs.
challenge.contractually_required: Commonly required by enterprise and bank contracts.
challenge.historical_convention: Annual third-party test with executive summary letter.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Secure Construction Standard rules (SEC-DB-001, SEC-UI-001, SEC-EXEC-001) aim to make classes of flaws unavailable by construction, within stated limits.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Per-release first-party assessment and architectural assurance matrix.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Construction evidence plus a smaller, deeper independent test focused on residual attack surface.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Only partially; construction claims need independent verification to be accepted.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Unknown; unvalidated. The prior agent judgment is kept in supporting_arguments.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: Interfaces that bypass restricted interfaces; claims of elimination without scoped evidence.
challenge.alternative_cost: High initial engineering; lower marginal testing cost later (unmeasured).

opposing_arguments: Customers and insurers expect an independent test regardless of architecture.

title: Right to audit and regulator access
status_rationale: No customer agreement template exists. Unbound requires auditor-ready evidence packages (SOC2-009). Banking and EU regulations expect institutions to secure audit and access rights over critical service providers.
target_answer: The agreement grants the customer, its auditors and its regulators the right to audit Echelon's compliance with its obligations once per year on 30 days' notice, and at any time after a security incident or regulatory request, with each party bearing its own costs unless the audit finds material non-compliance. Regulators receive access to records, personnel and systems as required by law (for example Bank Service Company Act examination authority over services to banks, DORA Article 30 for EU financial entities). Audit rights flow down to critical subcontractors where we can obtain them, and where we cannot (large cloud providers), we provide their independent reports. We offer audit evidence remotely through time-bounded, reproducible evidence packages to reduce fieldwork. Findings are remediated on agreed timelines and re-tested.
intended_practice: Include audit and regulator access clauses in the standard agreement; build evidence package export.
customer_statement: We expect to grant customers and their regulators audit and access rights. The contract terms and remote evidence packages are planned.

title: Internal audit, continuous control monitoring and evidence integrity
status_rationale: Unbound specifies continuous control monitoring and evidence requirements (SOC2-002, SOC2-004, SOC2-024, SOC2-027, SOC2-031) and a control register whose controls are all Designed with no operating evidence, tests or auditor review. Praxis produces attributable provenance and event records for repository work.
target_answer: Controls emit attributable, time-stamped, tamper-evident evidence as a byproduct of operation; a missing expected control heartbeat raises an exception; production evidence is labeled separately from test or synthetic evidence. Because there is no internal audit function, an external reviewer independent of the control operator tests a sample of controls semi-annually, and no control is verified solely by the person or AI agent that operates it.
current_practice: Not established for any operating service. Praxis provenance and event records exist for repository work only.
intended_practice: Implement continuous control monitoring for Unbound; engage external reviewer.
provable: Praxis repository provenance (actor kind, execution id) exists, which shows the evidence pattern but not operating controls.
customer_statement: Continuous control monitoring and independent control testing are planned. Echelon has no internal audit function.

challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Internal audit departments are infeasible for a tiny company; periodic sampling misses intermittent failures.

challenge.historical_convention: Internal audit function reporting to an audit committee.

title: Security documentation for customers subject to public records laws
status_rationale: No customer security documentation package exists, and no public-sector customer is planned or excluded. Records in this repository already carry a disclosure classification that could drive redaction.
target_answer: Echelon prepares each customer-facing security document in two forms: a full version for the customer's evaluators and a redacted version suitable for release under public records laws. Confidentiality markings identify the specific passages and the exemption claimed (for example security-sensitive information) rather than marking whole documents. The redacted version is generated from the disclosure classification on each record rather than edited by hand.
intended_practice: Generate full and redacted documentation sets from the disclosure classification fields when a trust center or documentation package is built.
customer_statement: Echelon does not yet have a security documentation package. It plans to provide full and redacted versions, with specific confidentiality markings, for customers subject to public records laws.
